utterances.text: Your Honour, inside our team or in between our teams with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe that's inside your teams because the changing of the counsel. Ms. Sinatra told Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Stojanovic told you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Stojanovic and I speak the same language and my B/C/S is much better than my English, so I doubt that there would be any miscommunication, but I will move on. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, Dr. Barr, I assume that you cannot do that examination here today for the rest of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN BARR
utterances.text: Not well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thanks a lot. I have one last set of questions. Is it possible to determine how old are various parts of handwritings in this - how do we call it - unofficial duty officer's logbook you examined, if one part is older than the other, only for a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN BARR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Examining the specimen given by Mr. Jokic, did you conclude that he tried to hide anything or his handwriting we can understand as honest as possible?

utterances.speaker: KATHRYN BARR
utterances.text: Yes, it looked to be natural, fluent handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Dr. Barr, we don't have any further questions. And we wish you a safe trip -- to have a better trip than yesterday when you came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct, Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have -- I'll take them in order. We have a document marked Prosecution 716. That's the first report of Dr. Barr on her handwriting comparison. Second, we have Prosecution 717, which is a second report of Dr. Barr, which was an expansion of that first report. Thirdly we have Prosecution 718, which is the third report of Dr. Barr. This is the recent one dated 27th of January, 2004. Prosecution 719, which is the CV of Dr. Barr. Prosecution 720, which we will not be tendering that. I'll move to Prosecution 722, which bears the ERN number 02096264, that's one page; that is a personal information form used by Dr. Barr in her handwriting comparison and analysis. Next a document marked Prosecution 723, these are the 11 pages of handwriting specimen recently provided for the purposes of Dr. Barr's third report. And after that we have a document marked Prosecution 724, and I believe that's 724/A through /K. And these represent some of the graphic comparisons of the questioned and known handwriting, which Dr. Barr had explained. And -- oh, yes, and finally we have the Prosecution 724 bis, and these are the same documents as Prosecution 724 but with red circles and numbers to indicate which letter or character she was explaining to the Trial Chamber. So the Prosecution would move to have these admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't have any objections. I do, however, as a point of clarification find it somewhat odd that an expert who would refuse on behalf of the Prosecution to examine a piece of document requested by the Defence, given that the Prosecution has the burden of proof at this stage. And I find it rather curious, and I -- perhaps I think this is something that the Court may wish to make an inquiry because it goes to the objectivity of the witness, You Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, my understanding, and the witness would know the best, but my understanding is that being asked to examine material for both sides is -- puts the examiner in a very potentially difficult situation. And it's my recollection that that was not their policy, having had a conversation about it. And so I think the conclusions or the suggestions by counsel are really, at this point, unwarranted. And I don't find any substance in them. But this witness of course may be able to answer any issues there are on that point, as I'm going on conversations I had with Ms. Sinatra and the office that she works for several months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, I think different legal systems have different rules concerning the expert witness. In some countries the expert is allowed to testify for both parties and some not. I think in this case we believe that the Defence team has the full opportunity to call their witnesses, expert witness, on that specific issue in a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- Just one point of clarification. The request was made the Defence to the Prosecution, therefore the Prosecutor was making the request of the expert. But be that as it may, I think that we are well aware of, and I want to stress this, even though it's not -- this is not a particular issue in my case right now, but the Defence has very, very limited funds. We are allocated 100 hours in total for all experts for our cases, and that's why I think there are times when the Defence asks Prosecution witnesses to, for instance, make those examinations. And so I think the Court needs to keep that in mind that we don't have the resources that we would normally like to enjoy under the concept of equality of arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that is another matter. If in your case you have some difficulties, please inform the Bench. We'll do our best to help you within certain limits. Well, Mr. Lukic, do you have any objections to the documents tendered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think at this stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And before we make the rulings, there's a clarification I would like to seek from the Prosecution. That document P724 is from the /A to /K. And document P724 bis is from the /A to /H. Is that right? Are they the same document or different documents? For the sake of the record, we would like to have a clear understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. The 724 is broken down into 724/A through /K. 724 bis is the same thing as 724, but in the case of case of 724/A, 724/B, 724/C, and 724/D, all of those 724 bis, they have on them the red circles drawn by Dr. Barr, together with a number indicating which circle -- to distinguish the circles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this matter is cleared up. So our ruling is that those documents are admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents to tender by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we don't have anything today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. It seems to me that the time you used for your testimony is much less than the time you travelled to The Hague, although usually they only take a one-hour flight. But we are greatly assisted by your testimony. The usher will show you out of the room. I hope this time on your way back you are much luckier than when you came here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, are there any other witnesses waiting for this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We have -- Mr. Brunborg is coming over from studies in the Middle East and he should be here this weekend and ready to go for Tuesday, as planned. And Dean Manning is here and ready to testify after Mr. Brunborg. So we don't have anybody to fill the small gap this afternoon, but we're on schedule and regarding the potential two new witnesses, I was able to speak to Mr. Jovicic, the RS liaison and he has assured me he will do all he can to get those folks here. And looking at the last week of February is the best possible time, perhaps sooner if we can make it sooner. Perhaps one thing to clear up, I misspoke yesterday, the Rule regarding reciprocal discovery and the Defence's obligation to provide reciprocal discovery to the Prosecution was recently deleted from the Rules. It's a little unclear where that puts us going back to our original agreement for reciprocal discovery. I've discussed this briefly with Mr. Karnavas and I don't think we'll have a problem sorting this out, and we'll continue to discuss it as you had mentioned. I apologise. I didn't realise that it -- as you know, these Rules tend to come and go at times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you mean that next week we only have two witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct. And Mr. Brunborg, I'm hoping, will not take more than a day on direct. And I know Mr. Karnavas is looking forward to cross-examining him. And he'll -- I haven't gotten an estimate from him yet. And I don't think Mr. Manning will take more than one day on direct either, though I'm speaking for Mr. Waespi and Ms. Issa, so I haven't got the latest information, but I think that's about right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any matters that the Defence would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
